subject: art-design
title: 3D & Mixed Media: Foundations
welcome_lead: Get hands-on with form — learn how sculptors build up and carve away.
meta_desc: GCSE 3D foundations: additive vs subtractive sculpture, key materials, maquettes.
final_note: Once you can name the process, you can plan in three dimensions.

concepts.def: Building up form by adding material.
Carving away material to reveal a form.
A small preliminary model of a sculpture.
An internal skeleton that supports a sculpture.
Mouldable earth that can be fired hard in a kiln.
Powder mixed with water that sets hard.

walkthroughs.body_html: Additive processes build a form up — coiling clay, wrapping wire, layering plaster. Subtractive processes remove material — carving stone, wood or soap. Many sculptors combine both, or cast from an additive model to make a permanent piece.

A maquette is a small test piece. It lets you check proportion, balance and silhouette before committing to expensive material at full scale. Photograph it from several angles — sculpture must read from every viewpoint.

Soft materials like clay or papier mache sag without support. An armature — usually wire, wood or a metal rod — runs inside the work to hold weight. Plan where joints and stress points fall before adding material.
